html:
Zaire was the name of the vast Congo state in Central Africa under Mobutu Sese Seko, from 1971 to 1997. The map uses it for the country across these years, from the Belgian Congo to today's Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The land had suffered the forced rubber regime of King Leopold II before Belgium took it over in 1908. Belgium trained very few Africans to govern.

  • 1960: independence, with Patrice Lumumba as prime minister. Mutiny and the breakaway of mineral-rich Katanga began the Congo Crisis. Lumumba was murdered in 1961.
  • 1965: Mobutu seized power, backed by the United States as a Cold War ally.
  • 1971: he renamed the country Zaire and pushed out colonial names.
  • 1974: the Rumble in the Jungle boxing match in Kinshasa.
  • 1996 to 1997: after the Rwandan genocide spilled across the border, a rebellion backed by Rwanda and Uganda drove Mobutu out.
  • 1998 to 2003: the Second Congo War drew in many African states and cost millions of lives, mostly through hunger and disease.

Its music, from OK Jazz onward, spread across the continent.
